This adds 7 extra all-reduce dispatches (56 total: 8×7 for main data + 7 for factors + 1 final) but enables all ranks to compute consistently without the division/multiplication pattern, reducing arithmetic operations.

strategies.name: Fused Buffer Preparation with Vectorized Scaling
strategies.desc: Batch all 8 scaling operations within each iteration into a single vectorized operation by constructing a (2048,) scale-factor tensor via torch.repeat_interleave, enabling element-wise multiplication instead of 8 separate block operations. Keeps 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute overhead and enables better fusion of the scale/unscale operations within each iteration's prepare-communicate-correct cycle.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level All-Reduce with Factor Accumulation
strategies.desc: Exploit the 224-rank world by organizing into 28 groups of 8 ranks (or 8 groups of 28). Perform intra-group all-reduce, compute factors locally, then inter-group all-reduce with factors, iterating 8 times. This changes the communication pattern from 8 global all-reduces to 8×2=16 smaller all-reduces with reduced per-dispatch payload or participant count, trading dispatch count for lower per-dispatch latency.

strategies.name: Pipelined Overlapped All-Reduce with Async Dispatch
strategies.desc: Split the 8 iterations into computation and communication phases that can overlap by dispatching the next iteration's all-reduce before completing the current iteration's scaling operations. Launch all-reduce on buf[iter+1] while computing f[iter] and performing division on acc[iter]. Requires careful buffer management (triple buffering across 3 tensors) but can hide some latency, maintaining 8 all-reduce dispatches with reduced wall-clock time.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition per Iteration
strategies.desc:
Replace each of the 8 all-reduce operations with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pattern (16 total collectives). Each rank computes factors only for its scattered portion (1/224 of data), reducing redundant computation by 224× per iteration. The all-gather then broadcasts the scaled results. This trades 8 all-reduce dispatches for 16 reduce-scatter+all-gather pairs but dramatically reduces per-rank computation of mean-square statistics.
